extracted.intended_audience: Scientists and scholars acting as ERC peer reviewers (Panel Chairs, Panel Members, Panel Evaluators, Remote Referees) for ERC Starting and Consolidator Grant calls
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for conducting the panel-based, two-step peer review (remote reviews, panel meetings, interviews) of ERC Starting and Consolidator Grant full proposals, covering evaluation criteria, scoring, conflicts of interest, reviewer responsibilities and required feedback to applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence is the sole evaluation criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific excellence is the sole criterion of evaluation and is at the core of the peer review evaluation process. It is applied to both the Research Project and the Principal Investigator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All assessments must be made against the evaluation criterion and its detailed elements alone. No other criteria (e.g., host institution standing, societal impact) must be considered. Incorrect application of the evaluation criterion is a procedural error and may justify re-evaluation. Evaluation questions are listed in Annex 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Project — Ground-breaking nature, ambition and feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Ground-breaking nature and potential impact: To what extent does the proposed research address important challenges? To what extent are the objectives ambitious and beyond the state of the art? To what extent is the proposed research high risk-high gain?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether objectives are novel (between or across disciplines), whether the project targets important challenges, and whether the risk/return profile is clearly articulated. The high-risk/high-gain nature should be acknowledged and assessed, and risk-management considered in the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Project — Scientific Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific Approach: feasibility bearing in mind high risk/high gain; appropriateness of methodology and working arrangements to achieve goals; involvement of novel methodology; adequacy and justification of proposed timescales, resources and PI commitment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At step 1 assess feasibility based on the Extended Synopsis; at step 2 assess methodology, timescales, resources and PI commitment based on the full Scientific Proposal. Look for appropriate methods, clear workplan, justification of resources and whether novel methodologies are proposed and feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal Investigator — Intellectual capacity and creativity
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent has the PI demonstrated the ability to conduct ground‑breaking research? To what extent does the PI provide evidence of creative independent thinking? To what extent does the PI have the required scientific expertise and capacity to successfully execute the project?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess PI's track record focusing on scientific content of outputs (preprints with DOI may be considered). Consider evidence of independence, creativity, and capacity to lead the proposed research. Apply DORA principles (do not use Journal Impact Factor). Consider Covid-19 impacts on CV where indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step-specific assessment (step 1 vs step 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Feasibility of the scientific approach is assessed at step 1; the detailed scientific approach (methodology, timescales and resources) is assessed at step 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At step 1 Panel Members as generalists review Part B1 (extended synopsis + PI CV/track record) and judge feasibility and ground-breaking nature. At step 2 Panel Members and Remote Referees review full proposal (Parts B1 and B2) including resources and budget; interviews with applicants are also taken into account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual review content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: During individual remote review reviewers must: provide a succinct explanatory comment for the Research Project; indicate extent of agreement with statements related to the excellence of the Principal Investigator (optional PI comment); and award marks for both Research Project and Principal Investigator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remote Referees (specialists) provide a qualitative three-option funding recommendation: highly recommended, recommended, not recommended. Individual reviews must be submitted by ERCEA deadlines. Reviews form part of the Evaluation Report given to applicants (for B- and C-scored proposals at step 1 and for all step 2 evaluations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring: numerical marks and panel scores
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers award numerical marks (integers or halves) ranging from 1 (non-competitive) to 5 (exceptional); panels produce final panel scores A/B/C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the full range of marks in general. Marks should be consistent with comments. Numerical marks are input to panel discussions but are not communicated to applicants; only final panel score (A, B or C) is provided in Evaluation Report. Panels use marks, reviews and discussion to reach rankings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 1 panel score definitions (A/B/C)
rubrics_metrics.description: Score A – the proposal is of sufficient quality to pass to step 2; Score B – the proposal is of high quality but not sufficient to pass to step 2; Score C – the proposal is not of sufficient quality to pass to step 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals within the budgetary cut-off up to three times panel's indicative budget are retained for step 2. Applicants receiving B or C may face resubmission restrictions per ERC WP. A-scored applicants are invited for interview at step 2; rejected proposals receive Evaluation Report including panel comment and individual reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 2 panel score definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Score A – the proposal fully meets the ERC's excellence criterion and is recommended for funding if sufficient funds are available; Score B – the proposal meets some but not all aspects of the excellence criterion and is not recommended for funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Step 2 assessment takes into account individual reviews, panel discussion and the interview with the applicant. Panels also analyse budgets at step 2 and may recommend justified reductions documented in panel comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality standards for individual reviewers' comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual reviews should be good quality, genuine, succinct but substantial, and impeccably polite. Comments should state and explain key strengths and weaknesses in light of the evaluation criterion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must provide substantial explanatory comments (not mere description), use dispassionate analytical and unambiguous language, grammatically correct sentences, constructive critical comments, ensure comments align with marks, avoid self-declarations of insufficient expertise, avoid references to applicant's age/nationality/gender/personal matters, avoid dismissive statements, be vigilant about unconscious bias and not penalise non‑conventional career paths, avoid comments on host institution or societal impact, avoid direct comparisons with other proposals or past assessments, avoid copy‑paste from proposal or other reviews, avoid comments on ethical/security aspects (these are handled separately), avoid budget recommendations at step 1 and avoid salary recommendations, and provide justification if recommending a budget cut at step 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest and confidentiality rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers must avoid situations where impartiality may be questioned; confidentiality is contractual and breaches can lead to termination. A list of conflicts is displayed in the online system and must be confirmed when accepting and when submitting the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conflicts include (non-exhaustive): being PI or team member in the proposal; involvement in preparation; direct benefit from acceptance/rejection; employment/contract with host or partner institutions in past 3 years; involvement in management of host/partner institutions in past 3 years; scientific collaboration with PI in past 5 years; mentor/mentee relationship; family or close personal ties; scientific rivalry/hostility; being a National Contact Point or working for EEN; member of a programme committee; any other situation precluding impartial review. Experts should not contact applicants or Host Institutions about the evaluation. Declared conflicts should lead to exclusion or reassignment ('out of room' or 'out of call').

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel comment requirements and distinctions
rubrics_metrics.description: The panel comment is the key element of feedback and must clearly explain the reason(s), respecting the ERC evaluation criterion, which make the proposal succeed or fail. It should reflect individual reviews, panel discussion and (at step 2) the interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel Members must ensure scientific recommendations to applicants are clearly distinct from budget recommendations to ERCEA (budget recommendations are binding). Panel comments should document important weaknesses revealed by discussion and must be conclusive and approved by the panel. Budget-related recommendations must be documented and explained in panel comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget review rules at step 2
rubrics_metrics.description: At step 2, the panel analyses the budget, its justification and requested contribution; recommendations for reduction may be made if some expenses (excluding salary costs) are not considered fully justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any recommended budget cuts must be documented and explained in the panel comments based on analysis of requested resources. Cuts across-the-board are not allowed; assessment is case-by-case. Avoid recommendations on salaries (they depend on national/institutional rules). Provide proper justification when recommending a budget cut.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of interdisciplinary / cross-panel proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Research proposals of a multi- and interdisciplinary nature are encouraged; interdisciplinary proposals are flagged and panels may request additional reviews from other panel(s). Applicants may indicate a second panel at submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial allocation to panels is based on applicant's expressed preference but may be changed by agreement of Panel Chairs for expertise reasons. Panels bear primary responsibility to ensure cross-panel proposals receive fair treatment; additional external expertise (Remote Referees or PEVs) may be sought where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissibility and eligibility reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Admissibility and eligibility are assessed by ERCEA, but experts who consider a proposal potentially inadmissible or ineligible should report immediately to ERCEA Scientific Officers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In some cases inadmissibility/eligibility may be confirmed during or after peer review. Experts should not make final admissibility decisions themselves; report suspected issues promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of reviewers and use of Remote Referees/PEVs
rubrics_metrics.description: Each proposal shall be reviewed by at least three peer reviewers. Remote Referees (usually 2–5 per proposal) provide specialist input, typically at step 2; Panel Evaluators (PEVs) can assist panels and perform remote reviews but do not attend panel meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remote Referees are non-paid, deliver individual assessments electronically and do not participate in panel meetings. Panel Chairs select remote experts based on expertise; any researcher worldwide may be nominated subject to accreditation and conflict checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and conduct during remote evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: During individual remote review there shall be no discussions of proposals between reviewers; Panel Members should not disclose assigned proposals to other experts. If a reviewer has insufficient expertise they must inform ERCEA Scientific Officers and the Panel Chair immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confidentiality is contractual. During the remote phase reviewers must keep proposals confidential and not attempt to contact applicants. Breach can lead to contract termination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roles and responsibilities of Panel Chairs, Panel Members and Lead Reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Panel Chairs and Panel Members are selected for specialist and generalist competence and must contribute concise, substantial reviews, participate fully in meetings, and may be asked to act as Lead Reviewer for assigned proposals. Lead Reviewer introduces the proposal at the panel meeting and drafts the panel comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel Chairs: chair meetings, attend initial/final chairs' meetings, reallocate proposals when necessary, assign proposals to reviewers and remote referees, ensure deliverables of required quality, select experts for remote evaluation. Panel Members: familiarise with all proposals, perform individual remote reviews of assigned subset, participate actively in panel meetings. Panels expected to work as entities with openness to interdisciplinarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ranking methodology and possible use of voting
rubrics_metrics.description: Panels rank proposals and may use successive elimination stages or discuss proposals in neutral/random order. While consensus is preferred, panels may use voting to expedite ranking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If voting is used it may be a majority vote with each Panel Member having one vote per proposal. A Panel Chair/Member under conflict of interest cannot be involved in discussion nor vote for that proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel deliverables and feedback to applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliverables of panel meetings include: ranked list of proposals; panel comments approved by the panel; list of approved Remote Referees (only at step 1); panel report; panel recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Evaluation Report to applicants contains: panel recommendation (A, B or C) and ranking range; panel comment; individual reviews. Applicants rejected at step 1 receive an information letter and Evaluation Report; applicants evaluated at step 2 receive an Evaluation Report after step 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements on language, tone and content of reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Use dispassionate, analytical, unambiguous language; grammatically correct complete sentences; avoid jargon; be constructive and polite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid dismissive statements, personal attacks, or references to non-relevant personal characteristics. Ensure comments are clear and helpful to applicants and consistent with marks and recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the SEP (online) evaluation tool and procedural compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Experts perform remote evaluations using the Commission's SEP evaluation tool and must follow SEP procedures and deadlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quick guide and detailed manuals/videos are provided (links in the guide). Experts must confirm conflicts in the online system when accepting and when submitting reviews, and comply with administrative/admissibility rules in the ERC Work Programme.
